title: Hostel Wi-Fi

examples.explanation: Put routers in the rooms at 1, 4 and 8 (or 1, 4 and 9). The closest two are 3 metres apart. No choice of three rooms keeps every pair 4 or more apart.

hints: Turn the question around: given a distance d, can you place k routers so that every two are at least d apart?
For a fixed d, sort the rooms and place greedily: take the first room, then the next room at least d past the last router, and so on. Why is taking the earliest possible room never worse?
If d works, every smaller distance works too. That monotonicity lets you binary search for the largest d that works.

complexity.time: O(n log n + n log X), X = 10⁹
